lines: One chunk holds at least 90.0 % of a page, so the browser fetches practically the whole page before it shows anything:
calendar-appointments-confirmation.js: 1 file, 3,565,983 B, and 3 chunks of 175,984 B its runtime loads later, of which calendar-appointments-confirmation.js is 3,565,983 B (95.3 %).
calendar-appointments-overview.js: 1 file, 3,265,663 B, and 3 chunks of 175,984 B its runtime loads later, of which calendar-appointments-overview.js is 3,265,663 B (94.9 %).

Code splitting puts what the first paint does not need behind a dynamic import, and then the browser fetches it when the code asks. Which part of a page that is does not follow from the build output; the source decides it.
1 package is imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

@nextcloud/vue: 1,733,988 B in 270 modules, 28.1 % of the static path of calendar-main.js, imported by its root in 78 files: components/AppNavigation/AppNavigationHeader/AppNavigationHeaderDatePicker.vue (NcButton), components/AppNavigation/AppNavigationHeader/AppNavigationHeaderNewEvent.vue (NcButton), and 76 more. It is imported per module as well, through 19 other specifiers.
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

32 components of @nextcloud/vue are delivered although no file in src names them, no other dependency names them and no component named by either imports them: 137,717 B, 2.2 % of the static path of calendar-main.js, next to 52 components the source names and 14 those pull in.
NcRichText 48,092 B, NcRichContenteditable 12,640 B, NcCollectionList 9,874 B, NcRelatedResourcesPanel 8,434 B, NcEmojiPicker 7,050 B, NcBreadcrumbs 6,364 B, and 26 more.
These arrive through the root import: under a barrel the whole component set is reachable, so the bundler must keep it. Per-component imports leave it free to drop what the app never names.

167 delivered files look like a webpack or CommonJS bundle. Their internal structure is not derivable from the artefact, so each counts as one file and the chunk figures below say nothing about what is inside them.
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
